correlates.name: Acute Tubular Necrosis (Medullary Ischemia)
correlates.presentation: Ischemic tubular injury in low-perfusion states (later lectures).
correlates.pathophysiology: Only 5-10% of renal blood flow reaches the medulla via the vasa recta — a deliberately low-flow design that keeps the medulla salty but hypoxia-prone.

correlates.name: Nutcracker Syndrome
correlates.presentation: Hematuria, left flank pain, pelvic pressure/pain, pelvic varicose veins, varicocele.
correlates.pathophysiology: Very rare compression disorder — the longer left renal vein is squeezed between the abdominal aorta and superior mesenteric artery as it crosses to the left kidney.

correlates.name: Renal Artery Stenosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Arterial narrowing reduces renal plasma flow while GFR is defended, so filtration fraction RISES.

correlates.name: Glucosuria in Diabetes Mellitus
correlates.pathophysiology: The filtered load of glucose exceeds the kidney's reabsorptive capacity, so glucose appears in the urine.

correlates.name: Chronic Kidney Disease
correlates.presentation: Know the CKD stages for exams — questions give symptomatology and expect stage 2 vs. stage 4. GFR calculators (kidney.org, MDCalc) linked for rotations.
correlates.pathophysiology: Progressive, permanent nephron loss, staged by eGFR.

correlates.name: Pre-Renal Failure (Pre-Renal Azotemia)
correlates.presentation: BUN:creatinine ratio greater than 20:1 with low urine sodium — the kidney works fine, it just is not being fed.
correlates.pathophysiology: An insult to the kidney's blood supply (arterial insult, dehydration, CHF). The kidney senses hypovolemia and sequesters sodium (urine sodium falls); slow tubular flow allows extra urea reabsorption — but creatinine is NOT reabsorbed.

correlates.name: Congestive Heart Failure and the Kidney
correlates.pathophysiology: Chronic low perfusion drives chronic sympathetic activation → sustained renal vasoconstriction and reduced renal blood flow.

correlates.name: Diabetic Nephropathy
correlates.presentation: Fatigue, bilateral pitting edema, hypertension, proteinuria WITHOUT hematuria, urine albumin 78 mg/g, creatinine 1.8, BUN 32, HbA1c 9.4%.
correlates.treatment: Tight BP and glucose control; SGLT2 inhibitor and/or ACE inhibitor/ARB; exercise, smoking cessation, low-sodium diet. Monitor eGFR, creatinine, electrolytes, urine albumin. Avoid nephrotoxic NSAIDs; counsel on dialysis/transplant. Goal: slow the declining GFR.

correlates.name: Goodpasture Syndrome
correlates.presentation: Hemoptysis, fatigue, dark urine, hypertension; RBC casts; crescents in Bowman's space on biopsy.
correlates.pathophysiology: Anti-type 4 collagen antibodies attack the glomerular basement membrane — the MIDDLE layer of the filtration barrier.

formulas.name: Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)
formulas.meaning: The volume of plasma filtered into Bowman space per minute — the single best indicator of kidney function, and the product of the filtration coefficient and the net Starling pressure
formulas.normalValue: About 120 mL/min, which is 20% of renal plasma flow and filters roughly 173 L per day

formulas.name: Clearance
formulas.meaning: The volume of plasma completely cleared of a substance per minute; comparing it to GFR tells you what the tubule did — equal means neither secreted nor reabsorbed, higher means net secretion, lower means net reabsorption
formulas.normalValue: Inulin clearance equals GFR exactly, which is why it is the gold standard marker

formulas.name: Renal Blood Flow (RBF)
formulas.meaning: Total blood reaching both kidneys each minute, delivering oxygen and nutrients; a high hematocrit raises viscosity and resistance and therefore lowers it
formulas.normalValue: About 1 L/min, roughly 20% of cardiac output, to organs that are only 0.5% of body weight

formulas.name: Renal Plasma Flow (RPF)
formulas.meaning: The cell-free plasma delivered per minute — the only part of renal blood flow that can actually be filtered
formulas.normalValue: 600-650 mL/min; estimated clinically as the clearance of PAH, which is cleared in a single pass

formulas.name: Filtration Fraction
formulas.meaning: The proportion of arriving plasma that gets filtered; it rises in dehydration and renal artery stenosis where GFR is defended as RPF falls, and drops in glomerular disease where GFR falls while RPF holds

formulas.name: Net Filtration Pressure
formulas.meaning: The balance of Starling forces across the glomerular capillary; only glomerular hydrostatic pressure favors filtration, while Bowman hydrostatic pressure and capillary oncotic pressure oppose it
formulas.normalValue: +16 mmHg, directed out of the capillary into Bowman space

formulas.name: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP)
formulas.meaning: The time-weighted average driving pressure for organ perfusion, weighted toward diastole because the heart spends more of each cycle there
formulas.normalValue: 70-105 mmHg systemically, falling to roughly 50-60 mmHg by the afferent arteriole

formulas.name: Excretion
formulas.meaning: The master balance sheet of the nephron: what leaves in the urine is what was filtered, minus what was taken back, plus what was added along the tubule
formulas.normalValue: Of 173 L filtered daily, 99% is reabsorbed and about 1.73 L is excreted

formulas.name: Filtered Load
formulas.equation: Filtered load = GFR x plasma concentration
formulas.meaning: How much of a substance arrives at the tubule per minute; glucosuria appears the moment the filtered load exceeds the reabsorptive capacity of SGLT2
formulas.normalValue: About 125 mg/min for glucose at a normal plasma level

formulas.name: BUN:Creatinine Ratio
formulas.meaning: Separates pre-renal failure from intrinsic disease — hypoperfusion drives sodium and water retention, urea follows the water back into the blood while creatinine does not
formulas.normalValue: Above 20:1 indicates a pre-renal pattern from dehydration, heart failure or arterial insult

formulas.name: Ohm's Law (renal flow)
formulas.meaning: Flow through any renal vessel equals the pressure gradient over the resistance, which is why the two arteriolar bottlenecks around the glomerulus control filtration so precisely
formulas.normalValue: A 20% occlusion can drive pressure from 120 to 293 mmHg at constant flow
